_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: As a deer longs for flowing streams, so we have come, thirsty for God.
Why are you cast down, my soul? Hope in God.
We came from the tombs and the noise, like the man Jesus set free.
He has clothed us, and given us back our right minds.
Out of the wind and the fire came a sound of sheer silence — the voice of God.
Speak, Lord; we are listening.
Come, let us worship, and tell what God has done.
We will declare how much God has done for us. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture a deer at the end of a long dry day, picking its way down to the streambed — that is your soul, thirsty, leaning toward living water.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise.
Some of us come worn down, like Elijah under the broom tree, ready to give up — and the angel says, get up and eat, the way is long.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise.
Some of us come like the man among the tombs, and Jesus speaks, and the chains fall, and we are in our right minds at his feet.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise.
So bring your thirst and your tears to the stream this morning. Drink deep, and tell the mercy you have found.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Thirsty as a deer for the stream, we come.
Hope in God.
From the tombs and the chains, Jesus has set us free.
Hope in God.
In wind and fire, a quiet voice still calls.
Hope in God.
Come, drink deep, and worship.
Hope in God, who is our help. Amen.
